- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent prices are falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +1.5+ points) — cap forecast at 1–2 points above recent peak.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model lags in correction — adjust forecast downward 0.5–1.0 point per sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5 points above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.3–0.7 points per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment — dampen forecast by 0.2–0.5 points if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
